t: The Act of July 6, 1968 (82 Stat. 294; 21 U.S.C. 114d–2 through d–6) is hereby repealed.

fable.w: This section only repeals an earlier statute; it creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. A tempting reading might speculate that the repealed Act involved outside parties, but the text itself establishes no process involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: The Act of July 6, 1968 (82 Stat. 294; 21 U.S.C. 114d–2 through d–6) is hereby repealed.

opus.w: The section only repeals an earlier statute (the Act of July 6, 1968). It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority or right to sue. A repeal is a federal action, but nothing here involves anyone outside the government in that action. Nothing in the text is on-topic, so the quoted span is empty.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply repeals a previous statute. It does not establish any process for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. There are no mentions of hearings, comment periods, advisory boards, or consultations. Therefore, it does not involve participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: The Act of July 6, 1968 (82 Stat. 294; 21 U.S.C. 114d–2 through d–6) is hereby repealed.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that repealing a law is a "decision" and therefore any prior process associated with the old law matters, or that the repeal itself implies some public input. However, the text provided is merely a statement of repeal. It contains no mechanism for public comment, consultation, hearings, or advisory committees. It is a legislative act of termination, not a procedural requirement for participation.
